readings.w: Lake's text, with the other witnesses (Lake's footnote names only A as adding)
readings.orig: τινὲς δὲ βοτάναι, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος ἐπικεκαύκει, ξηραὶ ἐγίνοντο
readings.en: some plants, whenever the sun had scorched them, became dry
readings.plain: And some plants dried up whenever the sun had scorched them.

readings.w: Athos manuscript (A, 1400s), as Lake's footnote reports: "A adds τὸ δὲ ὄρος τραχὺ λίαν ἦν βοτάνας ἔχον ξηράς"

readings.plain: And some plants dried up whenever the sun had scorched them. The mountain was very rough and had dry plants.

why: Lake leaves the added sentence out of his text. It repeats words from the fifth mountain ("rough," 78:7) and the dry plants just described, so it looks like a copyist's addition. The explanation in 98:1 does not mention roughness.

a: not cut from a quarry
t: "Not cut": Lake adds the "not"
p: A, the Ethiopic and the Latin read "cut." Lake adds "not" because 82:3 calls these same stones uncut.

readings.w: Lake's text, a correction of the three witnesses his footnote names
readings.plain: not cut from a quarry

readings.w: Athos manuscript (A), the Ethiopic (E) and the Latin (L), per Lake's footnote "μή om. AEL"
readings.plain: cut from a quarry

why: Lake's footnote: "μή om. AEL, but the addition seems to be made necessary by the reference in Sim. ix. 5, 3, where these stones are described as μὴ λελατομημένοι." In 82:3 Hermas asks about the stones from the deep that were "not cut, but went into the building just as they were," and only the stones from the mountains are said to be cut (81:5). The site follows Lake's correction, with this note so the reader knows that none of the witnesses Lake names has it. The verb latomeō is the stonecutter's word (86:2 has latomos, "stonecutter"); "from a quarry" is the site's plain English for it.

Lake says only that the numbers "do not quite agree" and that no hidden meaning has been found. The site follows Lake in each place, so the reader sees the disagreement the witnesses have.
b: Lake's footnote at 81:3: "κ΄ A, viginti quinque L, quindecim E." At 92:4: "κε΄ AL, xv E."
